b.answer:
Worked example: the Harvest Lane 2.1 scenario, with a filter on the link between Watch New Rows and Gmail.

Filter settingValue
LabelBig order or VIP
Condition group 11. total · Numeric operators: Greater than · 20000
OR group 21. vip · Text operators: Equal to (case insensitive) · yes

The two conditions sit in separate groups (click "Add OR rule"), not in one group, where they would both have to pass.

Test rowtotalvipEmail?
HL-T125,000yesYes (both)
HL-T225,000noYes (total)
HL-T39,000YesYes (VIP, case insensitive)
HL-T49,000noNo

Run once: Watch New Rows shows 4, Gmail shows 3. Credits: 1 check + 3 emails = 4; the filter is free.
mistakes: Putting both conditions in one group, which makes them AND, so only the row that is big and VIP sends.
Using a Text operator for total, so 9000 counts as "greater than" 20000.
Using the case-sensitive Equal to, so "Yes" fails where "yes" passes.
Testing only two rows instead of all four combinations.
b.pass: The filter shows two OR groups with a numeric total check and a case-insensitive VIP check, and a run of four rows (both, total only, VIP only, neither) sends exactly three emails.
b.redo: Send it back if the filter is AND, if a number is compared as text, or if fewer than four combinations were tested.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's 8 p.m. run with one Google Sheets · Add a Row to an Activity tab placed after the Not cancelled filter and before the router.

Activity columnValue
run_dateformatDate(now; "YYYY-MM-DD")
order_id, status, totalmapped from the Search module
routes_takenthe formula below
ifempty(trim(
  if(lower(1.status) = "paid" or lower(1.channel) = "standing"; "1 "; emptystring) +
  if(lower(1.status) = "new" and lower(1.channel) != "standing"; "2 "; emptystring) +
  if(parseNumber(1.total) > 50000; "3"; emptystring));
  "Fallback")
Orderroutes_taken
T11
T22
T32 3
T41 3
T5Fallback
T6(no row: stopped by the filter)

Five Activity rows for five non-cancelled orders, each once. Credits: 1 search + 5 log rows + 7 route actions = 13.

Why it's easier to maintain (three sentences). There is one log module instead of four copies, so a new column is added in one place. Every order is logged before anything can fail on a route, so the Activity tab is complete even when a route errors. The trade-off is that the formula repeats the route rules, so I copied each filter's wording beside its if() and change both together.

Submit: a screenshot of the scenario, the formula, the Activity tab after the six test rows, and the three sentences.
mistakes: Copying the log module into every route, which gives T3 and T4 two Activity rows each.
Logging after the router, which no longer exists as a single point because routes never merge.
Writing if() conditions that don't match the route filters (for example a case-sensitive "Paid"), so routes_taken is wrong.
Forgetting the fallback text, so T5's routes_taken is blank.
g.pass: After the six test rows, the Activity tab has exactly five rows (none for T6), each listing the right routes (1, 2, 2 3, 1 3, Fallback), with one log module in the scenario and a three-sentence explanation.
g.redo: Send it back if any order is logged twice or not at all, if a routes_taken value is wrong, or if the log module was duplicated across routes.
